answer: Gravedigger service record works as the check: graves dug at one churchyard across years of burials. A farm faking 413 aliases needs 413 separate verifiable records of this kind, each checked against the issuing authority, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. Call it the ledge rule: fakes pay per head, the honest pay once, the marble record is open for audit, and the raven window is too short for 413 aliases to earn their price back.
